sentences.text: This Civil Revision Petition is filed against the order dated 28.05.2015 in O.P.(Ele) No.204 of 2006 passed by the Court of the Additional District Judge- I, Kollam.
2. The revision petitioner is the petitioner in the original petition.

The original petition has been filed by the petitioner herein under Sections 10 and 16(3) of the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885 read with Section 51 of the Indian Electricity Act, 1910, seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd., for the trees cut and removed from her property for the purpose of drawing a 400 kV electric line/erecting tower from Madhura to Thiruvananthapuram.

entities.text: Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Three main issues raised in this revision petition are:-
A) The assessment of the value of the 2025:KER:74615 CRP NO.77 OF 2016 yielding trees is not in conformity with the settled principles.
B) There is error in the fixation of the land value.
C) The multiplier applied is wrong.
3. It is contended by the petitioner that the loss sustained due to the cutting of yielding trees is assessed not on the basis of any settled principles.
It is contended that the compensation for trees cut has been assessed based on surmises and not on the basis of materials on record.

4. As regards the fixation of land value, it is contended by the petitioner that the exemplar deed brought out in evidence which could have been the touchstone for determination of compensation payable for identically situated land was ignored by the learned District Judge and the market value of 2025:KER:74615 CRP NO.77 OF 2016 the property was fixed based on mere assumption.
On going through the impugned order, I find force in the said argument.
The fixation of land value is not based on materials on record.

5. With regard to the multiplier, it is contended that the learned District Judge has adopted '8' as the multiplier which is contrary to the law laid down by the Apex Court in Shaik Imambi v. Special Deputy Collector (Land Acquisition), Telugu Ganga Project [(2011) 11 SCC 639].

entities.text: Shaik Imambi v. Special Deputy Collector (Land Acquisition), Telugu Ganga Project [(2011) 11 SCC 639]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the said decision,
it has been held as follows:-
"6. The learned counsel for the appellant contended that the multiplier should not be less than 14 adopted by the Land Acquisition Officer.
We cannot accept the contention of the appellant.
Having regard to the consistent view taken by this Court, we are of the view that the High Court was right in holding that the multiplier should be 10.

This Court has repeatedly held that the standard multiplier should be 10; and that in special circumstances based upon specific evidence regarding the nature,
standard, condition of the orchard, the Court may apply a higher multiplier of 12 or 13 or a lower multiplier of Nalini.V vs Power Grid Corporation Of India Ltd on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144026376/
2 8."
2025:KER:74615 CRP NO.77 OF 2016 Thus, the multiplier adopted by the learned District Judge is contrary to the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Shaik Imambi (supra).
6.

[2023 : KER : 84945] which dealt with similar issues, the impugned order passed by the learned District Judge requires fresh consideration.

sentences.text: 7. I find that the learned District Judge has erred in fixing the value of trees as well as the land value.

Accordingly, the impugned order is set aside and the original petition is remanded for fresh consideration and disposal on the basis of evidence already on record and in the light of the observations made above.
The learned District 2025:KER:74615 CRP NO.77 OF 2016 Judge shall consider all relevant contentions raised by both parties and dispose of the original petition in accordance with law.

The parties are directed to appear before the Additional District Court - I,
Kollam, on 07.11.2025.
The learned District Judge shall endeavour to dispose of the matter within six months from the said date.
This Civil Revision Petition is disposed of.
